text.display: A lighthouse holds just one lamp, yet ships far out at sea can see it. How? On its own, a flame spills light in every direction, and most of it never reaches a ship. So Augustin Fresnel wrapped the lamp in rings of glass. The central rings bend the light into one straight beam. The outer prisms catch the steep rays, reflect them inside the glass, and add them to the same beam. Then the whole lens slowly turns, and far out at sea, sailors see the beam sweep past as a bright flash.
